subject: Guaranteed burst capacity request — Sunrise Bio

From: Elena Parkel <elena.parkel@sunrise.bio>

Cc: Sunrise Bio IT <it@sunrise.bio>
Date: Wed, 18 Jan 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: intermittent throughput drops during nightly batches — need guaranteed burst

Hi Marissa,

We’ve been seeing intermittent throughput drops during our nightly batch window (00:00–03:00 PT) since we migrated to the dedicated pool last quarter. During those windows our job latency moves from ~120ms/token to spikes >600ms for short periods, which causes downstream failures in our ingestion pipeline. We attached a small sample of the request logs for the last three nights (sunrise_throughput_sample_logs_q4.csv).

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a contractual guarantee for burst capacity during that nightly window (we want an explicit throughput guard for that 3-hour window)?
- If a guarantee is possible, what does the technical approach look like (reserved GPU set, priority queue tokens, pre-warm strategies)? Procurement (cc’d Daniel) will need clear SLA language and a draft addendum.

Ideally we’d get a short call this week to align on options — we’re targeting production runs single-region (us-west) and would prefer minimal code changes.

Thanks,
Elena Parkel
Head of Platform
Sunrise Bio

Subject: Re: intermittent throughput drops during nightly batches — need guaranteed burst

Hi Elena — thanks for the sample logs, they were helpful. Quick summary of what we see and three pragmatic options: 

What we observed (high level):
- Short-lived tail-latency spikes coincide with increased concurrency from large batched jobs hitting KV-cache warmup behavior.
- The dedicated pool is shared across tenants in your reserved SKU unless you take an isolated reservation.

Options we can offer:
1) Guaranteed reserved GPUs (isolated nodes): we allocate a small reserved pool for your account during the nightly window (e.g., 3 x A100-like accelerators). That pool is not available to other tenants and will eliminate preemption/context switching. Operational tradeoff: higher cost (monthly commit increase); straightforward contractual SLA (see addendum draft).

2) Priority lane + burst tokens: keep your existing reservation but provision a priority queue and pre-warmed runtime workers that consume burst tokens during the window (tokenized throughput guarantee). Lower cost than full reserved nodes, allows sharing outside the window. We can specify numeric throughput in tokens/sec for the window and tie credits when we miss the target.

3) Hybrid: reserved light pool + KV warmup optimization. Small reserved node set to cover the tail; plus runtime changes to aggressively pre-warm KV for your common prefixes before window start. This reduces required reserved capacity and cost. Requires a short instrumented rollout and a change in warmup behavior (no client code changes).

What I propose for the call:
- Walk through the hybrid option (3) as it’s often the best cost/latency tradeoff.
- If procurement wants contractual simplicity, start with option 1 and later optimize to hybrid.

I attached an initial addendum template for guaranteed burst language (redwood_dedicated_addendum_v1.docx) with suggested SLOs we can negotiate:
- 95th percentile token latency <= 250ms across the window;
- throughput floor of X tokens/sec (we’ll propose a number after we confirm your peak RPS);
- crediting formula: prorated monthly credit based on missed throughput minutes.

Notes / questions for Sunrise:
- What peak tokens/sec do you expect in the 00:00–03:00 window?
- Are you exclusively in us-west (preferred for placement)?

Call confirmed for Thu 11:00 PT (Marissa to send calendar invite) — I’ll prepare a short runbook and the draft SLA language.

Cheers,
Ben Carter

- Peak observed: ~1,200 tokens/sec sustained bursts (with micro-peaks to 1,600 tokens/sec) during the heaviest hour.
- We are single-region in us-west.

Procurement note (Daniel): we need explicit numeric guarantees and a simple credit formula. DocuSign process preferred; I can circulate the vendor-side contract once I have Redwood’s proposed addendum.

We’ll take the hybrid approach if the cost math works — reserved light pool + pre-warm sounds sensible. Can you surface a likely reserved-node count estimate for hybrid given 1,200 tokens/sec? Also please include an example credit calculation in the addendum.

Elena

Looping in Lauren from Legal so we can get contract language over to procurement quickly. Summary / ask:
- Account: Sunrise Bio (RWI-2027-0385)
- Agreed approach with customer: Hybrid reserved light pool + runtime KV pre-warm during 00:00–03:00 PT
- Customer peak: ~1,200 tokens/sec sustained (peaks 1,600) — single-region us-west
- Action items for Legal: addendum that includes:
    * Numeric throughput floor for the 3-hour window (we propose: 1,000 tokens/sec guaranteed, with an escalation path to expand reserved nodes if sustained shortfall > 3 days)
    * 95th percentile token latency target <= 250ms across the window
    * Crediting formula: for each minute below throughput floor, prorated credit = (missed_tokens / guaranteed_tokens) * (monthly reserved fee for the addendum period) * 0.5 (example included)
    * Term: 90-day pilot then automated review; ability to convert to full reserved-node commitment
- Attachments: initial addendum draft (redwood_dedicated_addendum_v1.docx) and sample logs provided by Sunrise.

Lauren — can you review the draft SLA text and send a redline back by EOD Monday so we can surface a DocuSign-ready version to Daniel? Ben — can you provide an estimated reserved-node count and a short cost delta for the hybrid (ballpark) by Monday as well — that will help procurement decide.

Thanks all — I’ll set up the follow-up call notes and invite if needed.

Best,
Marissa

Redwood Inference
